newsitem.title: CANADA: Greyhound Canada Q3 hit by competition.
newsitem.headline: Greyhound Canada Q3 hit by competition.

text.p: Greyhound Canada Transportation Corp said third-quarter results were hit by losses from its new air service, while it coped with lower bus ridership due to increased airline competition.

Earnings per share fell to C$0.12 from year earlier C$0.29 for the two-month period ended July 31. Greyhound reported two-month results since it is now carrying the transportation business of Greyhound Lines of Canada Ltd, and reconciled different year-end periods. The 1995 Greyhound Lines' results were restated for comparison.
Greyhound Canada said its air services had a pre-tax operating loss of C$1.3 million due to a shortened sales period. It launched its first flight on July 8.

Its bus division faced "a very heated competitive environment," the company said. Ridership fell by 8.5 percent since this year's start-up of a Western Canada no-frills air carrier called WestJet Airlines Ltd. The nation's major airlines, Air Canada and Canadian Airlines, matched WestJet's lower domestic fares.
Greyhound Courier Express said shipping volumes fell by 5.1 percent but this was partly offset by a 4.6 increase in rates.
